parts.name: Spar
parts.title: Sounding core
parts.blurb: A small storable tank. It will not survive a strap-on booster, and it will not lift a crew.

parts.name: Keel
parts.title: Small orbital core
parts.blurb: The smallest tank that can throw a kick stage at orbit. A pressure-fed engine will not lift it.

parts.name: Spine
parts.title: Medium core
parts.blurb: A wider tank. More propellant, more dry mass, and room for a hotter engine.

parts.name: Mast
parts.title: Heavy core
parts.blurb: The core you tool when one full-flow engine is finally in the stand.

parts.name: PS-80
parts.title: Storable, pressure-fed
parts.blurb: Nitrogen tetroxide and MMH. Low specific impulse, heavy, and the only engine you can buy this month.

parts.name: GG-620
parts.title: Kerolox, gas generator
parts.blurb: Kerosene and oxygen. The first engine that can lift an orbital core off this pad.

parts.name: SC-900
parts.title: Kerolox, staged combustion
parts.blurb: Oxidizer-rich staged combustion. More specific impulse than the gas generator, and a longer wait for the money.

parts.name: FF-1900
parts.title: Methalox, full-flow
parts.blurb: Full-flow staged combustion. Liquid oxygen and methane. This is the engine you are saving for.

parts.name: SRB, single
parts.title: One strap-on
parts.blurb: Asymmetric thrust. Without a gimbal the stack yaws off the pad. A Spar cannot take the load.

parts.name: SRB, dual
parts.title: Matched pair
parts.blurb: Two solids, symmetric. A cheap way to add thrust once the core is strong enough to hold them.

parts.name: Kick stage
parts.title: Storable upper stage
parts.blurb: A small hypergolic stage. It circularizes. Without it the stack comes back down.

parts.name: Fairing
parts.title: Payload fairing
parts.blurb: Uncrewed orbital payloads need the hammerhead. It comes off once the air is gone.

parts.name: Instrument cabin
parts.title: Autonomous
parts.blurb: Guidance, a transmitter, and a parachute for the payload. Not for people.

parts.name: Crew cabin
parts.title: Seats and a heat shield
parts.blurb: People, a window band, and a parachute. It is too heavy for the Spar.

parts.name: Fixed fins
parts.title: Four fins
parts.blurb: Enough to fly a lofted sounding shot. They do not bring a booster home.

parts.name: Grid fins, aluminum
parts.title: Recovery fins
parts.blurb: They steer in the air and they melt if max-q is high. Required for a recovery attempt.

parts.name: Grid fins, titanium
parts.title: Hot grids
parts.blurb: The same job as the aluminum set, through a hotter ascent.

parts.name: Body flaps
parts.title: Entry flaps
parts.blurb: Heavy flaps for a hot entry. They cut the propellant a landing burn needs.

parts.name: Gimbal
parts.title: Nozzle actuators
parts.blurb: Steering after the air thins out. The only cure for a single SRB.

parts.name: Landing legs
parts.title: Four legs
parts.blurb: Dead weight until the reuse program is funded and the booster still has propellant.

contracts.name: University sounding payload
contracts.blurb: 30 kg to 180 km. The only check that clears while the yard is empty.

contracts.name: Microgravity canister
contracts.blurb: 80 kg to 500 km. The Spar runs out of sky before this one is done.

contracts.name: LEO cubesat rideshare
contracts.blurb: 60 kg to a real orbit. Fairing, kick stage, and a core that can lift them.

contracts.name: Dual-manifest LEO
contracts.blurb: 900 kg to orbit. Same shape of flight as the cubesat, with a fatter check.

contracts.name: Crewed suborbital hop
contracts.blurb: A crew cabin to 80 km and a parachute home. The Spar is not strong enough.

contracts.name: House weather satellite
contracts.blurb: Your own bird, so the margin stays in the company. The office has to exist first.

contracts.name: Station truss delivery
contracts.blurb: 4 tons to a higher orbit. This is what the heavy core and the full-flow engine are for.

upgrades.name: Weld cell
upgrades.blurb: Jigs and a second shift. Cores and the kick stage cost 30% less to build.

upgrades.name: Reuse program
upgrades.blurb: A landing burn, a reserve of propellant, and people who have done it. The rocket still needs a gimbal, grid fins or flaps, and legs.

upgrades.name: Payload office
upgrades.blurb: Stop flying only other people's satellites. Unlocks the house weather satellite.

upgrades.name: Second pad
upgrades.blurb: The flame trench stops being the long pole. Turnaround drops from 12 days to 4.

upgrades.name: Station shop
upgrades.blurb: A module in the cradle and a contract to fly it. You need one orbit on the books before they will take the order.
